Avodah Zarah 4b:14.english: The Gemara presents a mnemonic for the ensuing statements of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi: Day, bear witness, strike, in the calf. The Gemara returns to the matter itself mentioned earlier (3a). Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi says: What is the meaning of that which is written: “Which I command you this day, to do them” (Deuteronomy 7:11)? “Today to do them,” but not tomorrow, in the World-to-Come, to do them. “Today to do them,” but not today to receive their reward, as reward is granted in the World-to-Come.

Avodah Zarah 4b:15.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi says: All of the mitzvot that the Jews perform in this world will come and bear witness for them in the World-to-Come, as it is stated: “Let them bring their witnesses that they may be justified, and let them hear, and say: It is truth” (Isaiah 43:9). He explains: “Let them bring their witnesses that they may be justified”; these are referring to the Jews. “And let them hear, and say: It is truth”; these are referring to the nations of the world.

Avodah Zarah 4b:16.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi says: All of the mitzvot that the Jewish people perform in this world will come and strike the nations of the world on their faces in the World-to-Come, as it is stated: “Observe therefore and do them; for this is your wisdom and your understanding in the eyes of the nations” (Deuteronomy 4:6). It is not stated: Before the nations; rather, the verse states: “In the eyes of the nations,” which taken literally teaches that the mitzvot will come and strike the nations of the world on their faces in the World-to-Come.

Avodah Zarah 4b:17.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi says: The Jewish people fashioned the Golden Calf only to give an opening for the claim of penitents, as it is stated after the revelation at Sinai: “Who would give that they had such a heart as this always, to fear Me, and keep all My commandments, that it might be good for them, and with their children forever” (Deuteronomy 5:26). If the nation was truly at such a lofty spiritual state, how could they worship the Golden Calf? Rather, their sin occurred so that it would be made clear that one can repent for any sin, as even a sin as severe as the Golden Calf was forgiven.

Avodah Zarah 4b:18.english: And this is similar to that which Rabbi Yoḥanan says in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai: David was not fit for that deed, and the Jewish people were not fit for that deed of the Golden Calf. David was not fit for that deed involving Bathsheba, as it is written: “And my heart is wounded [ḥalal] within me” (Psalms 109:22), i.e., King David had slain his evil inclination, and therefore it should not have been able to rule over him to that extent.

Avodah Zarah 4b:19.english: And likewise the Jewish people were not fit for that deed of the Golden Calf, as it is written with regard to the Jewish people of that time: “Who would give that they had such a heart as this always, to fear Me and keep all My commandments, that it might be good for them, and with their children forever” (Deuteronomy 5:26). Rather, why did the Jewish people do these sins?

Avodah Zarah 5a:11.english: The Gemara answers: Do not say that if our ancestors had not sinned we would not have come into the world, as we still would have been born; rather, it would have been as though we had not come into the world. We would have been of no importance, due to the previous generations that would have still been alive. The Gemara asks: Is this to say that if the Jewish people had not sinned with the Golden Calf then they would not have died? But isn’t the portion that addresses yivvum (Deuteronomy 25:5–10) written in the Torah, and the portion that addresses the inheritance a deceased father bequeaths to his sons (Numbers 27:8–11) is also written?

Avodah Zarah 5a:12.english: The Gemara answers: These passages were written conditionally, i.e., if the Jewish people were to sin and not become like angels, those halakhot would take effect. The Gemara asks: And are verses written conditionally in this manner? The Gemara answers: Yes, as this is what Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish says: What is the meaning of that which is written: “And there was evening and there was morning, the sixth day” (Genesis 1:31)? This teaches that the Holy One, Blessed be He, established a condition with the acts of Creation, and He said: If the Jewish people accept the Torah at the revelation at Sinai, all is well and the world will continue to exist. But if they do not accept it, I will return you to the primordial state of chaos and disorder.

Avodah Zarah 5a:6.english: Reish Lakish says: Come and let us be grateful to our ancestors who sinned with the Golden Calf, as had the ancestors not sinned, we, their descendants, would not have come into the world. Reish Lakish explains: As it is stated about the Jewish people after the revelation at Sinai: “I said: You are godlike beings, and all of you sons of the Most High” (Psalms 82:6), which indicates that they had become like angels and would not have had children. Then, after you corrupted your actions, God states: “Yet you shall die like a man, and fall like one of the princes” (Psalms 82:7).

Avodah Zarah 5a:7.english: The Gemara asks: Is this to say that if the ancestors had not sinned with the Golden Calf they would not have had children? But isn’t it written that Noah and his children were instructed: “And you, be fruitful, and multiply” (Genesis 9:7)? The Gemara answers: This instruction was issued only until the revelation at Sinai, but the Jewish people would have become like angels there, had they not sinned. The Gemara asks: Isn’t it also written about the Jewish people who were at the revelation at Sinai: “Go say to them: Return to your tents” (Deuteronomy 5:27), which means that they were instructed to resume marital relations? The Gemara answers: That verse is referring to the joy of the mitzva of marital relations, not to procreation.

Avodah Zarah 5a:8.english: The Gemara further asks: But isn’t it written: “That it might be good for them, and with their children forever” (Deuteronomy 5:26), which indicates that they would continue to bear children? The Gemara answers: This verse is referring to those children who stood with the Jewish people at Mount Sinai, not to future generations.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 4b:14:1.hebrew: ולא למחר לעשותם - שאין מצוות לעתיד:", "english": "“And not tomorrow to do them” – for there are no mitzvot in the future (the World-to-Come).

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 4b:17:1.hebrew: לא עשו ישראל את העגל - כלומר: גיבורים ושליטים ביצרם היו, ולא היה ראוי להתגבר יצרם עליהן; אלא גזירת מלך היתה לשלוט בם, כדי ליתן פתחון פה לבעלי תשובה, שאם יאמר החוטא: "לא אשוב, שלא יקבלני", אומרים לו: "צא ולמד ממעשה העגל, שכפרו ונתקבלו בתשובה":", "english": "“The Jewish people did not fashion the Calf” – meaning, they were heroes and masters over their inclination, and it was not fitting for their inclination to overcome them. Rather, it was a decree of the King for it to rule over them, in order to give an opening for penitents, so that if a sinner says: “I will not repent because God will not accept me,” they say to him: “Go and learn from the incident of the Calf, for the Jewish people acted heretically and yet were accepted in repentance.”

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 4b:17:2.hebrew: מי יתן והיה לבבם זה וגו' - בסיני נאמר; אלמא גיבורים ואמיצי לבב ביראתם היו:", "english": "“Who would give that they had such a heart as this, etc.” – This was said at Sinai; consequently, the Jewish people were heroes and strong-hearted in their fear of God."

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 4b:18:1.hebrew: לאותו מעשה - של בת שבע:", "english": "“[For] that incident” – of Bathsheba."

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 4b:18:2.hebrew: לבי חלל - יצר הרע חלל בקרבי, ואין לו כוח לשלוט בקרבי:", "english": "“My heart is wounded [ḥalal]” – the evil inclination was as though slain [ḥalal] within me, and it had no power to rule within me."

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 5a:10:1.hebrew: עד שיכלו וכו' - אוצר יש ושמו גוף, ומבראשית נוצרו כל הנשמות העתידות להולד ונתנם לשם:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 5a:10:1.english: Until they are finished, etc. – There is a storehouse whose name is Guf, and from the beginning of creation all the souls destined to be born were created and He placed them there.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 5a:10:2.hebrew: כי לא לעולם אריב - לאחר זמן הגאולה, "ולא לנצח אקצוף" מלגאול; כי רוח אשר לפני, נשמות שבגוף, יעטוף - הוא המאחר, כמו "העטופים ללבן" (בראשית ל׳:מ״ב); ונשמות שאני עשיתי:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 5a:10:2.english: For I will not contend forever – After the time of the redemption, "neither will I be always wroth" by refraining from redeeming; for the spirit which is before [Me], the souls that are in the Guf, "enwraps itself [ya’atof]" – it is that which delays, like [the word] "the late-born [ha’atufim] regarding Laban" (Genesis 30:42); "and the souls that I have made."

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 5a:11:1.hebrew: כמי שלא באנו לעולם - לפי שהן חיים לעולם, וכל זמן שהן קיימין אין אנו חשובין כלום:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 5a:11:1.english: As though we had not come into the world – Because they [the ancestors] would have lived forever, and as long as they were existing, we would not be of any importance.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 5a:6:1.english: To our ancestors – Those who made the Golden Calf.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 5a:6:2.english: We would not have come into the world – For they would have been like angels and would not have had children.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 5a:7:1.hebrew: לשמחת עונה - שעד עתה נאסר להן "אל תגשו אל אשה":
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 5a:7:1.english: To the joy of the [conjugal] time – For until now it was forbidden to them [as it says (Exodus 19:15)]: "Do not come near a woman."

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 5a:8:1.english: To those – Children who were already present during their standing at Sinai.

Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 5a:10:1.hebrew: אין בן דוד בא עד שיכלו נשמות שבגוף - ואם תאמר: מכל מקום יכלו על ידי עובדי כוכבים שיהו מולידים? ואומר הרב רבי אלחנן: דנשמות של ישראל ושל עובדי כוכבים אינן בגוף אחד. והא דאמר (שבת ל:): "עתידה אשה שתלד בכל יום" לימות המשיח - שמא יש לומר: גוף חדש ונשמות חדשות יהיו:
Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 5a:10:1.english: The son of David will not come until all the souls of the Body have been finished – And if you say: Nevertheless, they could be finished by the gentiles who would be siring children? And the Rabbi, Rabbi Elchanan says: That the souls of Israel and of the gentiles are not in the same Body. And as for that which [the Gemara] said in Shabbat (30b): "In the future a woman will give birth every day" in the days of the Messiah – perhaps it can be said that there will be a new Body and there will be new souls.

Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 5a:10:2.hebrew: כי רוח מלפני יעטוף - משיח נקרא רוח, כדכתיב (איכה ד׳:כ׳): "רוח אפינו משיח ה'"; והכי פירוש דקרא: המשיח מלפני יאחר, כמו "העטופים ללבן", על ידי נשמות אשר עשיתי:
Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 5a:10:2.english: For the spirit that enwraps itself is from Me – The Messiah is called "spirit," as it is written (Lamentations 4:20): "The breath [ru’aĥ] of our nostrils, the Messiah of the Lord"; and this is the explanation of the verse: The Messiah from before Me will delay, like "the late-born" regarding Laban, because of the souls which I have made.

Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 5a:6:1.hebrew: שאלמלא לא חטאו לא באנו לעולם - ואף על גב דאמרינן בפרק קמא דערובין (דף יג:): נמנו וגמרו "נוח לו לאדם שלא נברא" - היינו בתחלת לידתו, שאין ידוע מה יהא בסופו; אבל כשהוא צדיק - אשריו ואשרי הדור שהוא בתוכו. ועוד, דלמסקנא ד"כמי שלא באנו לעולם" אתי שפיר:
Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 5a:6:1.english: As had they not sinned we would not have come into the world – And even though we say in the first chapter of Eruvin (13b): "They were counted and they concluded: it is better for man not to have been created," that is at the beginning of his birth, when it is not known what his end will be; but when he is a righteous person, happy is he and happy is the generation in which he resides. Furthermore, according to the conclusion [of the Gemara on the next amud] that it is "as though we had not come into the world," it works out well.
